title: /import: inline mapping entries' `transform` (uppercase / lowercase / trim …) is accepted and silently ignored
body:
## What happens

`ImportRequestSchema.mapping` accepts the rich `FieldMappingEntry[]` form with `transform: 'trim' | 'lowercase' | 'uppercase' | 'lookup' | 'date_format' | 'none'`, `defaultValue` and `required`. `prepareImportRequest` (`packages/rest`) flattens an inline array mapping to `{ sourceField: targetField }` and drops everything else, so the request validates, the import runs, and no transform is applied.

## Reproduction (spec / rest 18.0.0)

```json
POST /api/v1/data/srm_supplier/import
{
  "format": "csv",
  "csv": "公司全称,国家 / 地区,统一社会信用代码\n示例公司,中国,91000000ma0trial02\n",
  "mapping": [
    { "sourceField": "公司全称", "targetField": "name" },
    { "sourceField": "国家 / 地区", "targetField": "country" },
    { "sourceField": "统一社会信用代码", "targetField": "credit_code", "transform": "uppercase" }
  ],
  "writeMode": "upsert", "matchFields": ["credit_code"]
}
```

The row fails the object's `^[0-9A-Z]{18}$` rule because the cell is still lowercase. Same for `transform: 'lowercase'` on an `email` column: `ZHOU@X.EXAMPLE.COM` and `zhou@x.example.com` are stored as two contacts, because `matchFields: ['supplier', 'email']` compares them case-sensitively.

## Expected

Either apply the entry's `transform` (and `defaultValue` / `required`) per cell before coercion, or refuse the request with a clear error that inline entries only support `sourceField` / `targetField`. Accepting it and doing nothing is the worst of the three.

## Impact in hotsrm

Legacy supplier ledgers carry lowercase credit codes and mixed-case emails. Today the import guide tells operators to clean these columns by hand before importing (temporary measure).

Found during the trial import for objectstack-ai/hotsrm#10.
